activities.label: TCP port scan (connect)
signals: One completed TCP handshake per open port (full connect, not a half-open SYN scan) — appears in firewall/flow logs and the service’s own connection log
Connections to many closed ports in a short window from one source — the classic horizontal-scan shape
activities.quieter: Scan only the ports the engagement needs, spread over time, from the authorized source; avoid full-range sweeps when a targeted set will do.

activities.label: Web content discovery (path brute-force)
signals: A burst of 404s (and the occasional 200/403) for paths a normal user never requests
High request rate from one source — the dominant web-scan tell
Requests for known-sensitive paths (/.git, /.env, /wp-config.php) that WAFs carry signatures for
activities.quieter: Use a focused wordlist seeded from robots.txt / sitemap / observed links, add jitter, and respect the app’s rate limits instead of hammering it.

activities.label: HTTP method / CORS / header probe
signals: OPTIONS requests and cross-origin GETs — uncommon from real browsers, so they stand out under review
Requests carrying an unusual Origin header (CORS test)
activities.quieter: A handful of targeted probes reveals the config; no need to sweep every method on every path.

activities.label: Web crawl (following the site’s own links)
signals: Ordinary GETs for real, linked pages — no 404 flood (that’s the brute-force tell), but the volume and cadence from one source stand out under review
Full traversal of the navigable site in a short window, including deep paths real users rarely open
activities.quieter: Cap pages and depth, pace requests with jitter, and let robots/sitemap seed the queue — a link-following crawl is already far quieter than path brute-force.

activities.label: Vulnerability checks (known-exposure probes)
signals: Requests for known-sensitive paths (/.git/HEAD, /.env, /actuator/env) — WAFs and SOC playbooks carry EXACT signatures for these, so each hit is conspicuous even at low volume
A probe Origin in the CORS check — uncommon from real browsers

activities.quieter: Keep the probe list curated and high-signal (content-verified), pace requests, and let page audits ride on pages already fetched instead of adding volume.

NONE at the app layer — idle windows are silent, so an ISP correlating entry/exit sees the engagement's activity windows. App-layer cover traffic would multiply request volume and is not implemented; DAITA pads flows but is not cover traffic either. Residual, stated, accepted

the TLS ClientHello of Node/undici governed HTTP is not a browser's (JA4-class distinguishability); not measured here — fporacle/shapegrade grade wire fingerprints on the C2 side, not this HTTP egress

governed VARVEL traffic is fail-closed inside the chain, but UNGOVERNED system traffic (other apps, OS, a browser outside the chain) bypasses ghost by design — split-tunnel and in-tunnel IPv6 are operator-side settings (Mullvad app), not observable from here

resistance to ISP-level entry↔exit flow correlation: LOW (single-hop, no shaper, no cover traffic). Multi-hop + VPN-layer padding (DAITA) raise the cost; NOTHING at the app layer defeats a national adversary holding both ends of the flow — and this platform never claims otherwise
